title: A customer created through the API without a term gets the default
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, working in {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • You have a valid Public API key for the test organization, the Public API documentation from the developers (it gives the request to create, update and read a customer), and a request tool.
    For example: Postman.
  • The shop's own term {Term-A} is the default for new customers.
    For example: {Term-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S10-11 Fourteen.
  • Names for two new customers, {Customer-A} and {Customer-B}.
    For example: ZZAUTOTEST S10-11 None and ZZAUTOTEST S10-11 Blank.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Send a Public API request that creates {Customer-A} with no credit term at all.
  2. Send a Public API request that creates {Customer-B} with an empty credit term.
  3. Open {Customer-A}'s customer page.
  4. Open {Customer-B}'s customer page.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the window closes and the new customer is saved.
  • Step 2: the window closes and the new customer is saved.
  • Step 3: the "Credit term" reads {Term-A}.
  • Step 4: the "Credit term" reads {Term-A}.

The tester sends a Public API request in this case. The exact request is added once the API documentation or tech plan is shared; until then the case is held.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11679 (Story 10, Imports and Public API)

  • S10-R2: “A customer created through the Public API without a credit term, or with a blank one, gets the shop's default.”
  • Key Decisions: “Imports and the Public API stay lenient. A blank term gets the default; a name matching any of the shop's terms (standard or its own, active or deactivated, ignoring capitals and spaces) is saved as that term in its correct spelling, and a deactivated one then shows as "{name} (Inactive)"; any other text is saved as sent and dated as today.”
